short: Complimentary items and cancelled bills, and the controls around them.
seoTitle: Comps and Voids — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: A comp is an item given free to a guest, usually for service recovery or hospitality. A void is an item or bill cancelled before payment.
definition: A comp is an item given free to a guest, usually for service recovery or hospitality. A void is an item or bill cancelled before payment. Both remove revenue from a sale that consumed stock.
bodyHtml:
Why Comps and Voids matters

Comps and voids are the classic route for revenue leakage, because a cancelled bill leaves no customer to complain. Unmonitored, they also make food cost look inexplicably high.

How Comps and Voids works in practice

Require a reason code and an authorising user on every comp and void, and review a weekly report by staff member. The pattern, not the individual entry, is what tells you something is wrong.

faq.question: Why track comps if they are good hospitality?
faq.answer: Because you still paid for the food. Tracking keeps it a deliberate cost rather than an invisible one.

faq.question: What is a warning sign in void reports?
faq.answer: Voids concentrated on one user, one shift or one payment mode, particularly after the bill was printed.
